P1.test: root gain reported by XGBoost (lambda=0, exact, prevalence intercept) vs Pearson X^2

P2.test: Monte Carlo mean of the root gain of a null split at fixed n_L vs n/(n-1)

P3.test: median best null split, n = 1e3..1e5, at each n_min (XGBoost defaults, prevalence intercept)
P3.rule: relative range across n <= 0.10 at every n_min
P3.measured: largest relative range of the median across n = 1e3..1e5: 0.045 (n_min 100); medians 1.81 to 5.34

P4.test: P(root uses the informative feature): XGBoost depth-1 fits vs the limit (4) by Monte Carlo
P4.rule: chi-square goodness of fit over cells, with the variance of each cell the sum of the binomial variance of the measurement and the Monte Carlo variance of the prediction: p >= 0.01; and mean absolute error <= 0.05. Exact search; hist reported conditional on (H1).
P4.measured: exact: 57 cells, chi-square 67.4, p = 0.16, mean |error| 0.034; hist (conditional on H1): chi-square 65.1 on 57 cells, p = 0.22, mean |error| 0.032

P5.test: incremental effect of log10 p on the root decision given s: logistic regression of the per-run root choice on a cubic B-spline of log s plus beta * log10 p (exact search), cluster-robust by cell
P5.rule: 95% CI of the change in win probability per decade of p lies within [-0.05, 0.05]
P5.measured: change in root win probability per decade of p at fixed s: -0.003 (95% CI -0.017 to +0.011; 57 cells, 5700 runs)

P6.test: no split in the first tree under the XGBoost 2.1 default intercept: identity (7) on each run's data vs XGBoost

P7.test: ensemble FNR (one-shot rule, prevalence intercept) vs root failure 1 - E[Q(M)^K], per informative cell
P7.rule: measured >= predicted - 2 SE in every informative cell
P7.measured: 33 of 33 informative cells at or above the root-split prediction (K = 5, hist grid); median excess +0.18

P8.test: paired difference FNR(smaller p) - FNR(larger p) at equal n_min, delta (E2, prevalence intercept)
P8.rule: difference >= -2 SE in every informative pair
P8.measured: 17 of 17 adjacent-p pairs with FNR(smaller p) >= FNR(larger p) - 2 SE; precision-weighted mean difference +0.040 (SE 0.010)

P9.test: pooled FPR of one-shot max-shadow rules with K = 10 (E4, E4b)
P9.rule: measured <= 1/(K+1) + 2 SE (data-set-clustered SE), for each method
P9.measured: FPR (SE) against 1/11 = 0.091: naive auto 0.081 (0.009); class weight 0.089 (0.010); downsample 0.075 (0.009); early stop 0.088 (0.010); oneshot gain 0.083 (0.009); oneshot total gain 0.076 (0.008); oneshot shap 0.091 (0.010); mwu shadow max 0.078 (0.009)

P10.test: hit rate of a null column with per-feature shadows, continuous and discrete cases (E10)
P10.rule: measured <= 1/(K+1) + 2 SE in every case and importance type
P10.measured: per-feature shadows: 9 of 9 case/importance pairs within the bound 1/7 = 0.143 + 2 SE; largest 0.155 (continuous, total gain). Boruta shadows, for comparison: largest 0.490 (continuous null among binary, total gain)

P11.test: ensemble FNR as K grows (E8): K = 5, 50, 200
P11.rule: FNR(K') >= FNR(K) - 2 SE for K' > K in every informative cell

P12.test: keep rate of irrelevant candidates after R rounds (E7) vs bound (10) and the limit bound 4 E[theta^2]
P12.rule: measured <= bound + 2 SE at every R; FPR at R = 60 <= 4 E[theta^2] + 2 SE

P13.test: Mann-Whitney FNR (shadow rule and BH q = 0.2) vs the prediction from N(sqrt(3 s_AUC / pi), 1) (E6)
P13.rule: within 0.05 + 2 SE in every informative cell
P13.measured: 12 of 12 informative cells within 0.05 + 2 SE; largest deviation shadow max, n_min 10, p 0.1: 0.71 vs 0.62

P14.test: Mann-Whitney keep rate of relevant columns (shadow rule and BH q = 0.1) under t3, log-normal and correlated-Gaussian features (E9) vs the s_AUC prediction
P14.rule: within 0.05 + 2 SE in every informative cell
P14.measured: 6 of 6 informative cells within 0.05 + 2 SE; largest deviation corr rel, bh 0.1, n_min 25: 0.72 vs 0.61

P15.test: sum of split gains vs leaf-sum identity (13) and Newton decrease (14), in the unit tests
P15.measured: max relative error: telescoping 1.4e-07, Newton decrease 2.2e-16 (10 trees)

macros.RunTime: The full set of experiments takes about 4 hours on four CPU cores, the longest being E4 (0.7 hours); every script also has a \code{--quick} profile for a fast smoke test.
